hypotheses.reasoning: notif-worker v4.29.0 processes notifications.outbound in batches with no prior errors. At 13:27:17 it threw an unhandled RangeError (call stack overflow) in expandReferences while processing msg-811112 at offset 567980 (#825). The process exited and restarted (#826). Each restart resumed at the same committed offset 567980 (#837, #866, #909) because the offset was never advanced past the bad message, so the consumer re-hit msg-811112 and crashed again (#844, #870). That is a crash loop on one message, which explains the CrashLoopBackOff and the growing notifications.outbound lag (#955, #1171, #1327, #1577, lag 1166 rising to 6004). Other services (notification-svc, template-svc, redis, api-gateway, notif-db) show no errors, so the trigger is isolated to this message's content (likely a self-referencing or excessively nested reference structure that overflows the recursive expander). The report-cron pandas ModuleNotFoundError (#545 onward, image report-cron:2026.10.2) is a separate, unrelated failure and is not the cause.

Alternative reading: the crash loop and lag growth could be read as backpressure amplified by restarts. However, the lag only grows because the consumer is stuck on one message; the amplification is a symptom of the poison message, not an independent trigger. The notification-svc slow-publish warnings are downstream impact only.

verdict.recommendedAction: Skip or quarantine the poison message msg-811112 (notifications.outbound offset 567980): move it to a dead-letter topic or manually advance the notif-worker consumer group offset past 567980 so the worker can drain the backlog. Then fix expandReferences to guard against cyclic or over-deep references (add a depth limit or iterative traversal) and add a try/catch that dead-letters a message instead of crashing the process. Inspect the producer of m-/msg-811112 to see why it contains such a structure. Separately, fix report-cron:2026.10.2 by adding the missing pandas dependency to its image; this is unrelated to the notif-worker incident.
